splits_note: There is no `test` split in this config. The bigbio loader maps the upstream JNLPBA Train archive to `train` and the upstream Eval archive to `validation`. The original 2004 shared task did not define a held-out validation set, so what most papers call the 'JNLPBA test set' is what HF returns under `validation`.
row_unit: ONE SENTENCE per row. Not one abstract. JNLPBA was annotated as IOB-tagged sentences and the bigbio_kb conversion preserves that grain. train.jsonl has 18546 sentences (from 2000 MEDLINE abstracts), validation.jsonl has 3856 sentences (from 404 abstracts).

native_files.origin: Two upstream archives from the NACTEM JNLPBA shared-task page, downloaded together and unpacked into the same flat folder (matches the layout you'd get by running `tar xzf` on both inside the same directory).

contents.Genia4ERtask1.iob2: Training data, 2000 MEDLINE abstracts, 5 entity classes (DNA, RNA, protein, cell_line, cell_type) in IOB2 format, no abstract boundaries.
contents.Genia4ERtask2.iob2: Same training data WITH abstract boundary markers between abstracts. Identical annotations to task1.
contents.Genia4EReval1.iob2: Evaluation/test data, 404 abstracts in IOB2 format, no abstract boundaries.
contents.Genia4EReval2.iob2: Same evaluation data WITH abstract boundaries.
contents.Genia4EReval1.raw: Evaluation text without tags (raw IOB2 input).
contents.Genia4EReval2.raw: Same raw text with abstract boundaries.
contents.sampletest1.iob2: 10-abstract sample test set in IOB2 format (a tiny subset for showing the format).
contents.evalIOB2.pl: Original Perl evaluation script for producing precision / recall / F1.
contents.README.txt: Upstream README describing the file layout and shared-task setup.

native_files.relationship_to_jsonl: train.jsonl is derived from Genia4ERtask1.iob2 (or task2 — same labels), validation.jsonl from Genia4EReval1.iob2 (or eval2). Provenance goes through the bigbio loader, which strips PMIDs and abstract grouping (each sentence becomes one JSONL row), and converts IOB labels to integer entity types per token.

id: Sentence id, an integer-as-string ('0', '1', ...). Globally unique across rows in the same split (not reset per abstract).
document_id: Always 'NULL'. The originating PMID is not preserved by this loader. To recover document grouping, use the upstream Genia4ERtask2.iob2 / Genia4EReval2.iob2 files in native/ which include abstract-boundary markers.
passages: Always []. There is no passage-level text in this config; the only text is inside the per-token entity rows.

entities._unit: ONE TOKEN PER ENTITY ROW. Each row in the sentence is emitted as its own entity, regardless of whether it is part of a real biomedical mention. To reconstruct entity *spans* you have to merge consecutive rows whose `type` follows the IOB pattern (B-X then I-X*).
entities.id: Token id, integer-as-string. Globally unique across rows.
entities.type: Integer-as-string IOB label index, '0' through '10'. Mapping (inferred from the data; the bigbio loader does not expose the names): '0' = O (outside any entity), '1' = B-DNA, '2' = I-DNA, '3' = B-RNA, '4' = I-RNA, '5' = B-cell_line, '6' = I-cell_line, '7' = B-cell_type, '8' = I-cell_type, '9' = B-protein, '10' = I-protein.
entities.text: Token surface text in a one-element list.
entities.offsets: Character span [start, end] but UNRELIABLE. The bigbio loader for JNLPBA computes offsets per token in a way that produces overlapping intervals within a single sentence (e.g. 'expression' at [21, 31] and 'and' at [25, 28]); they do not reliably index into any concrete sentence text. Treat these as positional hints only and use `text` for the actual surface.
entities.normalized: Always []. JNLPBA has no entity normalization.

caveats: This config is essentially the IOB token-tag data dressed up in bigbio_kb shape; the consistency with BC5CDR / NCBI Disease / BioRED is just cosmetic.
JNLPBA for sentence-level NER, the plain `jnlpba` HF dataset (with named B-/I-/O labels and clean per-token rows) would probably do, parallel with how we treat BC2GM.
